name: treesum-hidden
description: W1-a (E2, greenfield): treesum — the HIDDEN evaluator. Twelve contracts no arm sees: edge cases, error handling, idempotence and exit codes that a faithful implementation of docs/requirements.md must have; none of their inputs or expectations appears in the public task text or in the arms' bundle.

requirements.text: file_sha256 returns the SHA-256 of the file's bytes as 64 lowercase hex characters.
build raises NotADirectoryError for a root that exists and is not a directory, or does not exist.
loads ignores empty and whitespace-only lines, reads a final line without a newline like any other, and raises ValueError on a malformed line.
compare returns added, removed and changed, each a list of paths in ascending order.
build DIR prints the snapshot text, nested paths with / and entries in ascending path order, exit 0.
build DIR -o FILE creates or replaces FILE; a FILE inside DIR is not an entry of the snapshot.
verify prints one line per difference in ascending order of path and exits 1 when there is a difference.
Any other use exits 2 with a message on standard error and nothing on standard output.
Tests import nothing outside the standard library and treesum.

contracts.rationale: edge case: a file of zero bytes has the SHA-256 of the empty input; a reader that treats an empty read as an error, or hashes the path, fails
error handling: a root that is a file raises; os.walk and Path.rglob over a file silently yield nothing, so an implementation without the check returns {} instead
edge case: a leading empty line, a whitespace-only line and a final line without a newline; a parser that splits on newline and parses every piece fails
error handling: the digest field is not 64 lowercase hex characters; a parser that only splits on two spaces accepts it
every category non-empty, inputs in scrambled key order, two entries per list where order shows: lists must be sorted, an unchanged entry (a.txt) appears nowhere
nested directories two levels deep: relative paths joined with /, lines in plain string order of the whole path (a/b/c.txt before a/m.txt before z.txt), never directory-walk order
idempotence: the same build -o run twice leaves exactly one snapshot in FILE (5.3 replaces the previous content); an implementation that opens FILE in append mode doubles it

stdout.text:
added a/m.txt
removed old.txt
changed z.txt

contracts.rationale: exit code 1 with one added, one removed and one changed path, the lines in ascending order of PATH across the three kinds (not grouped by kind)
error handling: a FILE that cannot be read is a usage error — exit 2 and nothing on standard output; an uncaught FileNotFoundError gives a traceback and exit 1
exit code: an unknown subcommand exits 2, not 1 and not 0
the tests the agent adds import nothing outside the standard library and treesum (no pytest): counted by syntax over every .py under tests/

end to end, with the snapshot file inside the directory: build excludes it (two lines, not three), verify right after exits 0 (the self-exclusion is applied on both sides), a changed file makes verify exit 1, and the tool leaves the tree's other files untouched
